# 1 Samuel Chapter 3 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133r-133v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_003_page_001.jpg, 1SA_003_page_002.jpg

---

**3:1** And-the-lad Samuel [was]-ministering [to] YHWH before Eli. And-[the]-word of-YHWH was precious in-those days; there-was-no vision breaking-through.

**3:2** And-it-was on-that-day, and-Eli [was]-lying-down in-his-place, and-his-eyes had-begun to-grow-dim; he-was-not able to-see.

**3:3** And-[the]-lamp of-God had-not-yet gone-out, and-Samuel [was]-lying-down in-[the]-temple of-YHWH, where [the]-ark of-God [was].

**3:4** And-called YHWH to Samuel, and-he-said, "Here-[am]-I." [hinneni]

**3:5** And-he-ran to Eli and-said, "Here-[am]-I, for you-called to-me." And-he-said, "I-did-not call; return, lie-down." And-he-went and-lay-down.

**3:6** And-added YHWH to-call again, "Samuel!" And-rose-up Samuel and-went to Eli and-said, "Here-[am]-I, for you-called to-me." And-he-said, "I-did-not call, my-son; return, lie-down."

**3:7** And-Samuel did-not-yet know YHWH, and-not-yet [had the]-word of-YHWH been-revealed to-him.

**3:8** And-added YHWH to-call Samuel a-third-[time], and-he-rose-up and-went to Eli and-said, "Here-[am]-I, for you-called to-me." And-understood Eli that YHWH [was]-calling to-the-lad.

**3:9** And-said Eli to-Samuel, "Go, lie-down, and-it-will-be if He-calls to-you, and-you-shall-say, 'Speak, YHWH, for [your]-servant [is]-hearing.'" And-went Samuel and-lay-down in-his-place.

**3:10** And-came YHWH and-stationed-Himself, and-called as-time-by-time, "Samuel! Samuel!" And-said Samuel, "Speak, for [your]-servant [is]-hearing."

**3:11** And-said YHWH to Samuel, "Behold, I [am]-doing a-thing in-Israel which all [who]-hear-it, [the]-two his-ears will-tingle.

**3:12** In-that day I-will-raise-up against Eli all which I-spoke to his-house, beginning and-finishing.

**3:13** And-I-have-told to-him that [I-am]-judging his-house until forever, for-[the]-iniquity which he-knew, that [his]-sons [were]-bringing-a-curse upon-themselves, and-he-did-not rebuke them.

**3:14** And-therefore I-have-sworn to-[the]-house of-Eli: 'If shall-be-atoned [the]-iniquity of-[the]-house of-Eli by-sacrifice and-by-offering until forever.'" [i.e., the iniquity shall never be atoned]

**3:15** And-lay-down Samuel until the-morning, and-he-opened the-doors of-[the]-house of-YHWH. And-Samuel was-afraid to-declare the-vision to Eli.

**3:16** And-called Eli Samuel and-said, "Samuel, my-son!" And-he-said, "Here-[am]-I."

**3:17** And-he-said, "What [is] the-word which He-spoke to-you? Do-not-now hide [it] from-me. Thus may-God-do to-you and-thus may-He-add, if you-hide from-me a-word from-all the-word which He-spoke to-you."

**3:18** And-declared to-him Samuel all the-words, and-not he-hid from-him. And-he-said, "YHWH He-[is]; the-good in-His-eyes may-He-do."

**3:19** And-grew-up Samuel, and-YHWH was with-him, and-He-did-not let-fall from-all his-words to-the-ground.

**3:20** And-knew all Israel from-Dan and-unto Beer-sheba that [was]-faithful Samuel as-a-prophet to-YHWH.

**3:21** And-added YHWH to-appear in-Shiloh, for YHWH revealed-Himself to Samuel in-Shiloh by-[the]-word of-YHWH.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **3:1 -- "precious"** (יָקָר): The word means "rare, precious, costly." The sense is that prophetic revelation was rare/infrequent in those days. EMET preserves the literal meaning rather than smoothing to "rare."

2. **3:1 -- "vision breaking through"** (חָזוֹן נִפְרָץ): The Niphal participle of פרץ means "breaking through, spreading." The phrase means vision/prophecy was not widespread or common.

3. **3:3 -- "the lamp of God had not yet gone out"**: This detail anchors the narrative in time -- it was still night, before dawn, when the temple lamp would be extinguished. The lamp of God (נֵר אֱלֹהִים) burned from evening until morning (Exodus 27:21).

4. **3:4 -- hinneni** (הִנֵּנִי): "Here am I" -- this theophanic response echoes Abraham (Gen 22:1), Moses (Exod 3:4), and Isaiah (Isa 6:8). EMET transliterates this significant term.

5. **3:7 -- "did not yet know YHWH"**: The verb ידע ("know") here refers to experiential knowledge of YHWH through direct prophetic revelation, not intellectual knowledge of God's existence.

6. **3:10 -- "and stationed Himself"** (וַיִּתְיַצֵּב): The Hithpael of יצב implies YHWH took a position, stationed Himself -- suggesting a theophanic presence, not merely a voice. This is a remarkable theological statement about divine presence.

7. **3:13 -- "bringing a curse upon themselves"** (מְקַלְלִים לָהֶם): The Leningrad Codex reads מְקַלְלִים ("cursing/bringing curse"). The Masoretic tradition notes this as a tiqqun sopherim (scribal correction); the original may have read "cursing God" (מְקַלְלִים אֱלֹהִים), which was considered too blasphemous to preserve in the text. EMET follows the Leningrad Codex reading.

8. **3:14 -- oath formula with "if"** (אִם): The Hebrew oath formula uses אִם ("if") to express a strong negative: "If the iniquity shall be atoned..." means "the iniquity shall surely NOT be atoned." The apodosis is left unstated, a common feature of Hebrew oaths.

9. **3:15 -- "the doors"**: Samuel's duty of opening the temple doors indicates his role as a temple servant, consistent with his youth and his mother's dedication of him.

10. **3:18 -- "YHWH He is"** (יְהוָה הוּא): Eli's response is a terse expression of submission to divine sovereignty. The pronoun הוּא ("He") is emphatic.

11. **3:21 -- "by the word of YHWH"** (בִּדְבַר יְהוָה): This closing verse forms an inclusio with 3:1 ("the word of YHWH was precious"). The word that was rare has now found its vessel in Samuel.

-- EMET
